title: What SSVEC’s Mayday Drill Teaches Us - allhitskzmk.com
content: When you think of a first responder, you likely picture a police officer or a firefighter. But when emergencies involve downed power lines or damaged electrical grids, linemen are often the first on the scene. On September 22, Sulphur Springs Valley Electric Cooperative (SSVEC), alongside first responders, conducted a Mayday Emergency Response Training Drill to practice this exact coordination. How did the drill unfold, what skills were tested, and how did crews walk away feeling? The Mayday Emergency Response Training Drill simulated a field emergency involving a fallen power line on a vehicle, creating an electrical hazard that SSVEC crews had to secure before EMTs could extract the driver. Midway through the scenario, the complexity escalated when a lineman was struck by a vehicle. The evolving crisis gave SSVEC crews, 911 operators, firefighters, EMTs, and rescue teams the chance to practice communication, coordination, and medical response as the situation intensified. Police, ambulances, fire trucks, and an emergency helicopter were brought to the scene, and equipment such as stretchers, saws, axes, and grounding cables were used. The main goal of this exercise was for teams to establish clear communication and coordination as conditions on scene changed. Throughout the drill, crews worked together step‑by‑step, beginning with SSVEC linemen grounding the power lines so EMTs could safely reach the driver. Once the lineman was struck mid‑rescue, EMTs initiated medical care and called 911; fire crews assisted with extraction while 911 operators coordinated incoming units. SSVEC Senior Vice President of Operations Nathan Hodges explained the importance of these drills. It’s very beneficial to see it in action, and look for ways that we can improve and look for ways we are doing great so we can reinforce that. Safety is the foundation of every decision made in the field, and Mayday drills are designed to strengthen that commitment. By practicing high‑risk scenarios in a controlled environment, crews build the muscle memory needed to stay calm, communicate clearly, and act decisively when real situations unfold. These training exercises not only keep responders safe, but also ensure the community is protected when real emergencies happen. SSVEC Safety Manager Matt Riesgo said: Safety is the most important piece of what we do here. Exercises like SSVEC’s Mayday Emergency Response Training Drill highlight how much coordination goes into keeping the public safe during emergencies. For the community, these drills mean faster response times, safer rescue conditions, and teams who know how to work side‑by‑side when every second matters. title: Hey Burger is bringing it's award-winning flavors to Nic's Hometown Tavern in Hazlet, NJ - nj1015.com
content: Sometimes, you have to look at the little guys for the absolute best food and atmosphere. Yes, the big chains are great, but it's really the mom and pop kind of places that really bring our communities together. Nic's Hometown Tavern in Hazlet, NJ is one of those places. Despite so many bigger chains nearby, Nic's provides an atmosphere that many of those larger chains simply can't match. After paying a visit to their tavern, I 100% stand behind the description of calling it a hole in the wall kind of place. And in New Jersey, that's considered a very high ranking. But Nic's Hometown Tavern isn't alone. Five years ago, they joined forces with one of their former bartenders which ended up pushing themselves to the next level. Today, Nic's Hometown Tavern is home to Hey Burger. Yes, Hey Burger is it's own entity located within the tavern, but don't let that fool you into thinking that one isn't better than the other. In fact, Hey Burger enhances the tavern experience by providing a full menu of amazing burgers and more for it's customers. But not just any burger. They serve up award-winning burgers. Hey Burger has only been around for five years, yet they've already racked up tons of awards for their burgers which they proudly showcase within the tavern. Needless to say, they have a lot of support support from the community. Earlier this year, Hey Burger participated in the 2026 Jersey Shore Burger Playoffs, and won! Check out the video below from my visit last summer trying out one of their award-winning burgers. title: Now that fall is here, let's focus on eliminating expensive NJ beach badges before next summer arrives - nj1015.com
content: Well, we did it. Now that fall is here, it's another summer season in the books. And for the Jersey Shore, it's actually a glorious thing. That means local summer is here (for a little while longer, at least). Quieter beaches, less crowds, but yet, still plenty to do. And one of the best parts? The beaches are free once again. But before the summer of 2027 gets here, we should address something that Jersey Shore towns do not do (or if some do, there's far too few of them). Can we finally make the beaches free for Jersey Shore residents? Isn't this overdue? And to expand this even more, should we just do away with beach badges all together? Let's first ask the main question. Should we eliminate beach badges all together beginning the summer of 2027? Other states have figured out how to maintain their beaches without tags and seem to be managing just fine. Should New Jersey finally figure out how to do this? Personally, I'm not really sure. I think it's such a part of how we manage our beaches that it would be too hard to do away with. As for how we'd make up the shortfall? Probably raise taxes, which is something nobody wants to see. I mean, they're high enough as it is, so why raise them even more. So with the idea of eliminating beach tags in New Jersey pretty much a nonstarter, what about eliminating them for locals? Can't we at least do that? I've often argued that people who live right at the beach that requires badges shouldn't have to pay to step foot on the sand. I mean, they pay enough in taxes, why not just let them have free access year round? How do you feel about it? Should locals have free access to the beach they live at year round? Or should we finally get rid of beach tags forever? Additionally, how should we raise the revenue necessary to clean our beaches year round in the absence of beach badges? It's something to think about as we say farewell to the summer of 2026. The above post reflects the thoughts and observations of New Jersey 101.5 weekend host & content contributor Mike Brant. Any opinions expressed are his own.

title: TSMC Gains as Packaging Moves Closer to Its Suppliers - TradingView
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing TSM, the world's largest contract chipmaker, anchored a new Kaohsiung industrial park designed to tighten the link between advanced-packaging development, testing and workforce training. The U.S.-listed shares gained approximately 0.6% to $447.86, extending investors' focus beyond wafer fabrication and deeper into the packaging bottleneck shaping the AI-chip boom. TSMC plans to occupy two buildings at the site, including a laboratory and training center, with operations targeted for the fourth quarter of 2029. Industrial facilities will cover 53.6 hectares of the 88.7-hectare park, roughly 60% of the total area, giving equipment and materials suppliers space to test technologies closer to TSMC's qualification process. That matters because packaging is becoming a bigger part of the performance race as increasingly complex AI accelerators require tighter integration of chips, memory and substrates. The valuation picture adds another angle. At $447.86, TSMC trades 23.32% above its GF Value estimate of $363.17, showing how much future growth investors are already pricing into the shares. The Kaohsiung project could shorten the path from supplier innovation to production approval, but it should not be mistaken for an immediate capacity surge: TSMC disclosed no investment figure, output target or customer commitment. For now, the story is about faster qualification and a stronger packaging ecosystemnot instant volume. Select market data provided by ICE Data Services. Select reference data provided by FactSet. title: Rochester Breaks Ground on New Features at Silver Lake Skate Park - Kat Kountry 105
content: A couple of months ago, my 12-year-old son came up, hesitated for a second, and said, "Dad, don't be mad... but I've been emailing the city council and mayor." Immediately I thought, why are you bugging these busy people? But then I asked to read the emails. Seeing how polite and articulate he was made me very proud, and the news that came out today is going to make him very happy. In his email to city leaders, my son referenced an open letter I wrote to the 'potheads and punks' at the Rochester skate park. He also shared some ideas and asked when the project would start. Mayor Norton responded to thank my son for reaching out and connected him with the parks department. Paul Widman, Director of the Rochester Parks Department, read the email and responded with a note saying, "We are moving forward with renovating the skatepark. I believe the concerns you shared are included in the updates." City Councilman Dan Doering also sent a note saying he'd be an advocate during the design process. I wanted to mention those people by name because they could have easily ignored my son's email, but they took the time to respond, and I know my son appreciated that very much. On to the good news... On Tuesday, the City of Rochester sent a press release announcing the start of the skate park expansion. See the construction timeline below. Fencing is up around the active work zones, but skaters can still use the rest of the facility throughout construction. Crews will work through the fall, pause for the winter, and pick back up in spring 2027. The skate park expansion is expected to be completed by the middle of next summer.

title: Ramsey Canyon's Spring-fed Creek And Sycamores Offer Cooler Refuge In The Huachuca Mountains Near Sierra Vista - allhitskzmk.com
content: I used to judge a good weekend by how much activity I had packed into it. Seeing concerts, going to clubs, nonstop visits with friends and family—all seemed like the measure of a time well spent. These days, a good weekend for me is a break from the busy grind and everyday stress. Getting away from it all doesn’t have to mean a long drive and an expensive weekend away. Cochise County is full of places to unplug, take a deep breath, and enjoy some of Arizona's most beautiful scenery. I live close to the Huachuca Mountains and watch the sunset turn to honey and drip behind these Thunder Mountains. Because they’re so close, it’s easy to take them for granted, but they’re also an easy getaway. Nestled in the Huachuca Mountains is Ramsey Canyon Preserve. A short drive from downtown Sierra Vista, the area is known for cooler temperatures, shady trails, and remarkable biodiversity of the unique sky islands. This ecological crossroads, where mountain and desert ecosystems meet, creates habitats for hummingbirds, deer, and countless other species. A spring-fed creek and towering sycamores make it feel worlds away from the surrounding desert. title: A Major Federal Court Case Is Unfolding in Great Falls - KSEN AM 1150
content:
A pretty significant federal court case is happening right here in Great Falls, as a judge has ordered 24 people to be released from immigration detention. U.S. District Judge Brian Morris ordered the release of 24 people being held at the Cascade County Detention Center after determining that they had been unlawfully detained by federal immigration officials. Some of those people had been in custody for more than six weeks. The case started back in July when Jesus Verde Hernandez was arrested by federal immigration officials near Lewistown without a warrant. A judge later determined that the government had not shown enough evidence to justify a warrantless arrest. That case then snowballed into a larger class-action lawsuit involving several other people who had been arrested without warrants and were being held in Montana. According to Upper Seven Law, attorneys filed 37 individual petitions seeking the release of people who were still being detained. The government agreed that 24 of those people were in circumstances similar to two earlier cases where the judge had ordered releases. Daily Montanan is reporting that there are still 13 people being held while the federal government makes additional arguments about their individual cases. The court is considering those requests on a rolling basis. The Cascade County Detention Center has also been dealing with a critical staffing shortage. Earlier this month, the sheriff's office announced emergency changes to reduce the jail population to a level that could be safely managed with the available staff. That included ordering ICE and CBP detainees to be picked up and removed from the facility. Montana

title: Louisiana Made a National Fall Views List — Hale Boggs Bridge at #108 and Kisatchie at #128 - 107 JAMZ
content: LOUISIANA - The autumn equinox has come and gone, so we are officially in Fall here in South Louisiana. And boy, doesn’t it feel like fall — with all those leaves changing colors and that cool weather in the air? No, we don't have the beautiful fall foliage like you'll see in the Northeast. For now, the cool temperatures are limited to a brief overnight period. However, pumpkin spice everything is abundantly available at every coffee shop on every corner, so there's that. But let's forget all that and embrace the joys Fall brings, like good vibes and, in some places, good views. The travel company Exoticca set out to find the most breathtaking Autumn views in America. They surveyed 3,012 people and, based on their personal experiences, asked about the best vantage points to witness nature's annual spectacle. READ MORE - Best Running and Walking Trails in Lafayette: Complete Distance and Difficulty Guide for Every Level What about the rest of the list? Well, there were a total of 134 spots across America that were part of it, and Louisiana did have two places that made the cut. Hale Boggs Memorial Bridge between Destrehan and Luling was voted #108 nationally, followed by Longleaf Vista Trail in Kisatchie National Forest checked in at #128. #108 Hale Boggs Memorial Bridge, Mississippi River (Destrehan-Luling) - Spanning the Mississippi River between Destrehan and Luling, the Hale Boggs Memorial Bridge offers sweeping views of the river and its wide, working corridor. In late fall, subtle shifts appear along the banks, with cypress and bottomland hardwoods edging into muted yellows and russet tones. While the bridge is more known for its dramatic span than bold foliage, the long river vistas take on a different character under autumn skies. #128 Longleaf Vista Trail, Kisatchie National Forest - Located in the Kisatchie Ranger District, the Longleaf Vista Trail offers a unique perspective on Louisiana's fall foliage. As the only national forest in the state, Kisatchie features diverse landscapes, including pine forests and hardwood bottoms. During fall, the hardwoods along the trail display subtle hues of yellow and red, especially in the Longleaf Vista area. The trail provides hikers with a serene environment to observe the changing leaves, listen to the sounds of nature, and enjoy the crisp autumn air. The combination of towering pines and colorful hardwoods creates a picturesque setting for outdoor enthusiasts. So, there you go; we do have a little something to look at for fall views in Louisiana. Although we're not too sure about the Hale Boggs Memorial Bridge. It looks like just a big ol' bridge to us. The Longleaf Vista Trail, that might hold a little something cool to see.

title: ZAWYA: QORE enters Egypt’s real estate market with $577mln investment plan through 2030 - TradingView
content: Egypt - QORE has officially entered Egypt’s real estate development market, unveiling Maydan, its first project in 6th of October City, as part of an investment plan targeting EGP 30bn through 2030. The company said its entry into real estate development builds on more than 30 years of experience in construction, infrastructure, and manufacturing. It plans to leverage capabilities across these sectors to develop and operate real estate projects in Egypt. QORE has also signed partnerships with Inversion, Hafez Consultants, and TSM Asset Management for the development and operation of Maydan. Under the agreements, Inversion will provide advisory services related to the project’s development and investment strategy, while Hafez Consultants will handle engineering consultancy and design. TSM Asset Management will oversee asset management, operations, commercial activities, and retail strategy. Construction work on Maydan has already begun, according to QORE. The company said its EGP 30bn investment plan will be supported partly through internal financing, with self-funding expected to cover between 30% and 40% of construction costs. Maydan is being developed on approximately 10,000 sqm of land, with a total built-up area of around 30,000 square metres and a targeted development period of three years. The mixed-use project will include commercial spaces, administrative offices, and medical clinics. QORE said the project will also include an operational and service component targeting companies and factory owners, offering commercial, administrative, accounting, and tax-related services. Medhat Sayed Abdel Hafiz, CEO of QORE, said the company’s entry into real estate development represents an expansion of its existing activities in construction, infrastructure, and manufacturing. Mohamed Diab, CEO of Inversion, said the company’s role would focus on planning and development strategy, including the project’s mix of uses and operational model. QORE is part of a wider group comprising 19 companies operating in Egypt and abroad across construction, infrastructure, manufacturing, and related activities. The group has worked on more than 100 projects in Egypt and the region and employs more than 1,555 professionals, according to the company. Its activities include general contracting, ready-mix and precast concrete, aluminium manufacturing, architectural systems, and interior solutions. The group’s previous projects include 500500 Hospital in Sheikh Zayed City, the Dr Hassan Mostafa Sports Halls Complex in 6th of October City, Nasser Institute, and the High Court of Appeal at the City of Justice. Mohamed Hafez, CEO and Chairperson of Hafez Consultants, said the company would focus on the engineering and architectural design of Maydan, taking into account its combination of commercial, administrative, and medical uses. Mohamed Galal, Chairperson of TSM Asset Management, said the company would develop the project’s operations and retail strategy, including the mix of activities and services. QORE said its expansion plans through 2030 include developing a portfolio of projects in Egypt and evaluating additional investment opportunities, particularly in 6th of October City. Potential projects include a land plot of approximately 20 feddans in the Al-Thawra area and another plot of less than 20 feddans in Boulevard, the company said. © 2026 Daily News Egypt. Musk said in 2019 that Tesla could have one million Robotaxis on the road by the end of 2020, a target that never materialized as Full Self-Driving (FSD) remained a supervised system. title: GlobalFoundries Drives Gross Margin Expansion: Can the Momentum Last? - TradingView
content: GlobalFoundries Inc. GFS is making steady progress in strengthening its profitability. The company delivered stronger-than-expected second-quarter 2026 results, supported by favorable business mix, manufacturing productivity gains and higher utilization. In the second quarter, gross profit increased 24% to $505 million, while IFRS gross margin expanded to 28.3% from 24.2% in the year-ago quarter. Non-IFRS gross margin was even stronger at 29.9%, representing a 470-basis-point year-over-year increase and a 90-basis-point sequential improvement. Technology services, which includes IP, licensing, software, reticles and nonrecurring engineering activities, accounted for approximately 11% of second-quarter revenue. Solid traction in the Technology services business is expected to be a strong driver of Gross Margin in upcoming quarters. The company is also benefiting from stronger demand in communications infrastructure and data centers. Revenues from this end market surged 62% year over year in the second quarter, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. High-margin technologies such as silicon photonics and silicon germanium are also gaining momentum. Apart from improving revenue mix, margin expansion is also driven by structural manufacturing-cost improvements and greater utilization of existing manufacturing capacity. Despite the favorable momentum, sustaining the improvements will depend on GF’s ability to balance profitability and investments in future growth. GFS needs to continue moving toward higher-value technologies while improving manufacturing productivity to sustain margin growth in the long run. GlobalFoundries operates in a highly competitive foundry industry. It faces competition from industry giants, such as United Microelectronics UMC and Taiwan Semiconductor TSM. UMC's gross margin increased to 32.5% in the second quarter of 2026 from 29.2% in the first quarter and 28.7% a year earlier. UMC’s growth was driven by higher wafer shipments and better capacity utilization. In the second quarter of 2026, TSM’s gross margin reached 67.7%, up 150 basis points sequentially and 910 basis points from the year-ago quarter. Management attributed the sequential improvement primarily to cost-improvement initiatives and higher capacity utilization. GFS has increased 44.1% over the past year compared with the industry’s growth of 34.6%. title: Steel Framing And Roof Completed For New Greylock School In North Adams - WUPE
content: Since this project is in my neighborhood, I've been following the progress of Greylock School's new future home in North Adams. I have to say, it's really coming along since the project started months ago. While I never actually attended this school, this project brings back memories of 2011, when my old high school, Hoosac Valley, was being renovated. The steel structure and roof were recently completed, and the new school is finally taking shape. iberkshires.com reports that Todd Ashford, a representative with the owner's project manager, Colliers International, said at the recent School Building Committee meeting that nearly all the steelwork is complete. title: RPU Used Police Drones to Find Storm-Damaged Power Lines - KROC-AM
content: Rochester, MN (KROC-AM News) - Rochester Police Department drones assisted RPU as crews worked to restore power to thousands of Rochester homes and businesses in the aftermath of the powerful storm that hit the region in the early morning hours of September 2. Rochester Public Utilities General Manager Tim McCollough, during his regular monthly appearance with Andy Brownell for RPU Unplugged during Rochester Today on News-Talk 1340 KROC-AM and 96.9 FM, discussed the use of law enforcement drones to pinpoint the properties where downed trees and tree limbs had created power outages. Listen to the entire interview by clicking on the link below. Rochester Public Utilities General Manager Tim McCollough joins Andy Brownell for RPU Unplugged and discusses the response to a recent severe storm that left more than 10,000 RPU customers without power. McCollough explained how the deployment of the police drones dramatically sped up the process of finding the sources of the hundreds of power outages that affected Rochester after 70-mile-per-hour winds raked across the community. He noted that, in the past, nearly all of that work had to be accomplished by RPU crews driving through the affected areas and even walking through backyards to locate downed trees and tree limbs. He says the outages caused by the storm affected almost 11,000 RPU customers. While the vast majority of those customers had their power restored during the afternoon of September 2, he says others faced a very frustrating situation of having to wait many additional hours to get their power back. READ MORE: Olmsted County Declares Local Emergency After Sept. 2 Storm According to McCollough, the widespread damage caused by the storm overwhelmed RPU's outage reporting system, which caused headaches for numerous RPU customers seeking to report that they were without power and to learn when they might expect it to be restored. McCollough says RPU is reviewing its response to the outages and will be applying the lessons learned in the future. He says that includes improving communication with affected customers during a mass outage event. READ MORE: RPU to Begin 3-Year Water and Electric Advanced Meter Upgrade New Electric Meters Could Speed Up Future Outage Response McCollough noted that the ongoing deployment of advanced electric meters throughout the RPU system will alleviate many of the challenges faced by the municipal utility in its response to outages. He says the new meters will allow RPU to instantly identify customers impacted by outages and speed up the repair process.

title: TSMC Reports 30% Sales Growth In May, But Stock Remains Under Pressure Over Potential Taiwan Chip Curbs - Stocktwits
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. shares remained under pressure in overnight trading ahead of Wednesday, as upbeat monthly sales failed to lift sentiment amid concerns over potential new chip export restrictions. TSM dropped 1.3% after gaining 0.3% in the regular session on Tuesday. Earlier in the day, Bloomberg reported, citing its sources, that Taiwan is considering stricter export controls on AI chip sales to China to further align with U.S. measures. The proposed rules would strengthen authorities' ability to act against the illegal rerouting of advanced AI hardware, including Nvidia’s servers, to China, where such sales have required the U.S. government approval since 2022. Later, in the early hours of Wednesday, TSMC issued its monthly update. Revenue in May increased 30% to NT$416.98 billion ($13.2 billion), with combined April and May sales up around 24% from a year ago, according to Bloomberg calculations. Analysts expect sales growth of 35% in the second quarter, which ends in June, according to estimates from Koyfin. The latest performance shows steady demand for advanced chips, which power data centers and other systems that power AI applications, smartphones and automobiles. TSMC makes cutting-edge semiconductors for the likes of Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices. The biggest buyers of those chips – including cloud companies Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft – have set aside $725 billion for AI-related investments this year. In April, the Taiwanese giant raised its full-year sales guidance and said its capital spending should trend toward the upper end of an existing forecast range of as much as $56 billion in 2026. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for TSM remained ‘bearish’ for a second day, with some traders arguing that the stock is expensive. TSM stock has gained 41% year-to-date and currently trades near an all-time high. Last month, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced that the U.S. chip designer would set up a headquarters in Taiwan and invest up to $150 billion annually in the region. The plan is expected to bring additional capital and resources into the region, potentially boosting business for TSMC and other contract chipmakers that support the company’s AI supply chain. Starbucks (SBUX) stock extended its rally overnight as the company reportedly evaluates strategic alternatives for its Japan operations, including a potential partial divestment or public listing. The update comes as the coffee giant simultaneously pursues an ambitious long-term expansion strategy across the United States and overseas markets. According to a Bloomberg report, the Seattle-based company has begun early conversations with financial advisers as it assesses the best path for its Japanese unit, one of its largest international markets. Japan is one of Starbucks' largest markets, with about 2,100 stores. Unlike many other international markets, Starbucks owns and operates most of its stores in Japan rather than licensing them to partners. The report indicated that a partial divestment could place the value of the Japanese operation between ¥400 billion and ¥500 billion, equivalent to approximately $2.5 billion to $3.1 billion. The review follows Starbucks' recent restructuring efforts in Asia. Earlier this year, the company completed the sale of a 60% interest in its China retail business to Boyu Capital, a move management described as supporting long-term, disciplined expansion. Starbucks’ stock inched 0.6% higher overnight, heading into Wednesday. Speaking at the Evercore Consumer & Retail Conference on Tuesday, CEO Brian Niccol said the company sees considerable overseas runway, with roughly 22,000 stores outside the United States. Niccol said he remains optimistic about Starbucks' future in China and believes the business can grow well beyond its current size. As Americans grapple with record levels of credit card debt, SoFi Technologies (SOFI) CEO Anthony Noto is touting personal loans as a clearer path out of debt than high-interest revolving credit cards. In a post on X, Noto said that even as credit cards keep people in debt “because the math is stacked against them,” personal loans are “a responsible alternative.” The comments come amid recent data from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York that showed total U.S. credit card balances topped $1.25 trillion in the first quarter of 2026, up from $1.18 trillion a year earlier, notching the highest first-quarter level in 15 years, and the most since the 2008 financial crisis. Meanwhile, U.S. credit card delinquencies have surged to a 15-year high, with 13.1% of credit card balances now 90 or more days overdue. Noto said that high credit card interest rates can cause repayments to balloon for years, even with almost no principal reduction. “Many borrowers pay mostly interest just to keep the line open,” he said. Data from the New York Fed shows that average interest rates have climbed up to 21%, higher from 14.6% in February 2022. Forbes Advisor’s weekly credit card rates report as of early this week pegs the current average credit card interest rate at 25.18%. Meanwhile, personal loans, with their fixed term, fully amortizing, and single-digit interest rates, help with balance reduction amid “no surprise carry cost, no open-ended timeline, no incentive for balances to linger,” Noto said. “This makes personal loans a responsible alternative because it’s an option that actually helps them move towards being debt-free,” he emphasized. In his comments on social media, Noto also highlighted how SoFi has helped its members pay down more than $40 billion in credit card debt over the past decade. “We want to give people a real exit from debt with competitive, fixed-term and clear timelines,” he said. In its first-quarter results, SoFi’s total loan originations reached a record of $12.2 billion, up nearly $1.7 billion from last quarter. Personal loan originations also topped a record $8.3 billion. In the quarter, the company also rolled out the Personal Loan Doc Coach powered by AI with the aim to streamline the loan application process. The company’s recently-launched AI-powered financial assistant, SoFi Coach, also helps users tackle debt by combining financial mathematics with behavioral psychology. Brian Walsh, head of advice and planning at the digital bank, said in an interview with Banking Dive that the assistant is trained to present guidance in ways that encourage action using tailored recommendations to help users make financial decisions, including paying down debt more effectively. In its latest quarterly results announced in late April, SoFi posted a revenue increase of 41% to a record $1.1 billion. The financial company also noted record loan originations, member growth of 35% to a record 14.7 million members, as well as product growth of 39%. (NIO) slid 4% in overnight trading ahead of Wednesday as investors weighed the EV maker's overseas expansion after fresh industry data showed exports remained a tiny fraction of overall sales despite the company's ambitious overseas plans. Nio’s U.S.-listed stock fell over 3% on Tuesday to end at 5.28, its lowest level in over two weeks. Data from the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) showed that Nio exported 88 vehicles from China in May across its three brands: Nio, Onvo, and Firefly. While that was double April's 44 units, exports represented just 0.23% of the group's 37,705 deliveries during the month. The company's global deliveries surged 62% from a year ago in May to their highest monthly level of 2026. In the first five months of 2026, Nio exported 403 vehicles, up from 315 in April and ahead of year-ago levels. However, exports account for just 0.27% of the 150,526 vehicles the company delivered globally during the same period. Earlier this year, Nio co-founder Qin Lihong said the company aims to deliver "several thousand" vehicles overseas in 2026 while preparing for broader international expansion over the next few years. At the current pace, annual exports would remain well below that target. CEO William Li has also said that the company plans to operate in 40 countries and regions by the end of the year, up from 20 at the end of 2025. Nio's recent export growth was driven by Firefly, the group's compact EV brand that the EV maker has positioned as its spearhead for international expansion. Firefly shipped 59 vehicles overseas in May, up from just seven in April. The brand has expanded beyond its initial launches in Norway and the Netherlands into markets including Belgium, Denmark, Austria, Portugal, Singapore and Thailand. In May, Firefly exported 189 vehicles, nearly matching Nio's 195-unit total and accounting for almost half of the group's exports this year. The export rebound comes as Firefly continues to gain traction domestically. The brand delivered 5,663 vehicles in May, up 14% from April and 54% from a year earlier. Nio also unveiled a limited-edition Firefly "Pixel Player Special Edition" on Wednesday, a retro gaming-themed model limited to 333 units and priced 13.4% above the standard version as the company looks to attract younger buyers, CnEVPost reported. The premium Nio brand exported 24 vehicles in May, down 27% from April. The ES6, marketed overseas as the EL6, was the brand's top-exported model, followed by the ES8 and the ET5 Touring. Exports also included a small number of ET5 sedans and ET9 flagship sedans. Notably, most shipments are heading to newer markets such as Uzbekistan, Costa Rica and Armenia rather than Nio's established European markets. The company previously said that European customers will not receive the latest model refreshes until late 2027, while it transitions the region toward a distributor-led structure to reduce costs. Meanwhile, Onvo's overseas footprint remains even smaller. The sub-brand exported just five vehicles in May, including four L60 SUVs and one L90. Through the first five months of the year, Onvo exported only 19 vehicles. The brand remains heavily focused on China, where deliveries jumped to 12,029 vehicles in May after the launches of the L80 and refreshed L90. title: New Detour Starts Monday on Hwy. 30 Southwest of Rochester Airport - KROC-AM
content: Rochester, MN (KROC-AM News)- A new detour is set to start Monday on a Rochester-area highway. Crews began working on the highway in August by resurfacing the road, replacing other culverts and improving drainage. MnDOT anticipates that the detour to be in place until October 9.

title: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing stock gains as AI demand lifts margins and guidance - AD HOC NEWS

Ltd. stock (ISIN US8740391003) is trading around USD 434.67 as of September 20, 2026, reflecting the market’s confidence in its dominant position in advanced chip manufacturing and strong AI-driven demand for its leading-edge nodes.Pluang highlights that the shares are up about 41.1 percent over the recent period, markedly outperforming broader semiconductor peers and the S&P 500. A key catalyst for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing stock in September 2026 is the company’s commanding share of the global foundry market in Q2 2026, driven largely by AI chip demand from major customers such as Nvidia and other hyperscalers.Ground News reports that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing captured about 73 percent of global foundry revenue in Q2 2026, with quarterly sales near USD 40.2 billion for the period. According to TokenPost on September 9, 2026, market researcher TrendForce estimated that the top ten foundries generated about USD 53.49 billion in Q2 2026 revenue, up 11.5 percent quarter on quarter, with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing accounting for approximately USD 40.2 billion of that total. The same report notes that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing’s Q2 2026 gross margin reached about 67.7 percent and its operating margin about 60.3 percent, underscoring the profitability of its advanced manufacturing platform compared with many peers. The first is capital intensity: maintaining leadership at 3-nanometer and below nodes requires sustained capital expenditure in the tens of billions of US dollars over multiple years, which can pressure free cash flow in periods when demand normalizes. Reports on the foundry industry for Q2 2026 emphasize that while Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing’s margins are currently robust, the cost of expanding capacity in Taiwan, the United States and other regions remains high relative to many competitors.TokenPost A second key risk is geopolitical: as a Taiwanese-headquartered company with critical facilities on the island, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing is exposed to cross-strait tensions and broader regional security dynamics. title: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing's Foundry Market Share Is a Massive Moat Nobody Talks About - The Globe and Mail
content: TSMC makes chips for nearly every leading big tech firm. Analysts expect strong growth from the company next year. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing(NYSE: TSM) is well known for having a massive market share in the chip manufacturing world. It partners with nearly every artificial intelligence (AI) computing company and also with non-AI computing companies: Apple is historically its largest client (although that could shift this year). The reality is that TSMC has built an unassailable moat, and that gives it protection against losing its competitive advantage. Missed AI’s "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we’re only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » A moat is one of the investment characteristics that investing legends like Warren Buffett have advised investors to seek. I think TSMC's moat comes from its sheer size, and it has locked several clients into using its services as a result. Image source: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company. The reality is that demand for logic chips, the type of chips TSMC produces, has never been higher. The AI build-out created a brand-new demand wave for chips. During the second quarter, 66% of TSMC's revenue came from its high-powered computing segment, which encompasses AI demand. Prior to the AI build-out, its largest segment was smartphones. This massive increase in AI chips has caused TSMC's business to swell, and it's unlikely to give up any of those gains. The reality is that no competitor can take TSMC's market share because no competitor has the capacity. According to industry analyst company TrendForce, global chip foundry revenue was more than $50 billion in the second quarter. TSMC owned about 72.5% of total revenue during the quarter. The second-place company owned 5.9% of the market, so it's pretty obvious that TSMC is the largest player in this space by far. While TSMC could lose some market share, it's going to be nearly impossible for other companies to steal a lot. The reason is the massive cost required to build enough production capacity to break down the size advantage that TSMC has created for itself. This makes TSMC a fantastic stock pick, and fortunately for investors, it's still trading at the lower end of its recent valuation ranges. The AI build-out has been going on for a few years, which gives investors some historical data to work with. Near the end of 2024 and 2025, TSMC's stock topped out at about 29 times forward earnings. Now it trades at about 25.4 times forward earnings. If TSMC could rise to 29 times forward earnings before the year is over, that would provide about 14% upside. That's a great return in a very short time and gives investors a reason to buy the stock right now. Next year should also be a strong year, as Wall Street analysts are forecasting 35% revenue growth. With TSMC trading at a reasonable price range now and 35% growth possible for next year, it should easily outperform the market from now until the end of 2027. The AI build-out not expected by many analysts to slow until the end of the decade. That leaves several more strong years for TSMC as an investment. Investing in TSMC is one of the best ways to take advantage of the massive AI build-out, as it isn't a bet on any one computing unit. Instead, it's a bet that we're going to need more advanced chips in greater quantities, which seems highly likely. Given how much production capacity TSMC has right now, it's unlikely that any competitors will be able to steal a meaningful amount of its market share, giving the company an unassailable moat that protects its competitive advantage.
